source_evidence.observation: The problem is to find the polynomial p_n of degree at most n interpolating data f_j at distinct points x_j for j=0:n; the interpolation points and evaluation point x are fixed while f varies, and vector inequalities are componentwise. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, Section 2 opening paragraph]
The exact Lagrange representation is p_n(x) = sum_{j=0}^n f_j ell_j(x), where ell_j(x) is the product of (x-x_k)/(x_j-x_k) over k=0:n with k != j. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, equation (2.1)]

For p_n(x) != 0, cond(x,n,f) is the limit as epsilon tends to zero of the supremum of |(p_f(x)-p_{f+Delta f}(x))/(epsilon p_f(x))| over perturbations satisfying |Delta f| <= epsilon|f|. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, Definition 2.1]
The paper explicitly states that n in cond(x,n,f) records dependence on the interpolation points x_j. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, sentence following Definition 2.1]
Lemma 2.2 gives cond(x,n,f) = (sum_{j=0}^n |ell_j(x)f_j|)/|p_n(x)| and states that this quantity is at least 1. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, Lemma 2.2 and equation (2.2)]
For any Delta f satisfying |Delta f| <= epsilon|f|, the lemma states |p_f(x)-p_{f+Delta f}(x)|/|p_f(x)| <= cond(x,n,f) epsilon. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, Lemma 2.2 second display]
The proof states that the upper bound is attained by Delta f_j = epsilon sign(ell_j(x))|f_j| and derives the result from linearity in the data. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, proof of Lemma 2.2]

Section 2 supplies a condition number for later error analyses, and the paper's stability notions perturb function values but not interpolation points. [PDF p. 1, printed p. 547, Section 1 final paragraph]

The floating-point model, unit roundoff u, and rounding-error constants are introduced only in Section 3, after Definition 2.1 and Lemma 2.2. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 549, Section 3 standard floating-point model paragraph]

binders: The data are indexed by j=0:n, so f consists of n+1 indexed values f_0,...,f_n. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, Section 2 opening paragraph and equation (2.1)]
The interpolation points x_0,...,x_n are distinct and fixed. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, Section 2 opening paragraph]
The evaluation point x is fixed. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, Section 2 opening paragraph]
The data vector f varies, and Delta f ranges over componentwise perturbations constrained by |Delta f| <= epsilon|f|. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, Section 2 opening paragraph and Definition 2.1]
In the condition-number definition, the supremum over admissible Delta f is taken for each epsilon inside the limit epsilon -> 0. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, Definition 2.1]
hypotheses: p_n is the polynomial of degree at most n interpolating f_j at the distinct x_j for j=0:n. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, Section 2 opening paragraph]
Definition 2.1 and Lemma 2.2 operate under p_n(x) != 0, as required for their relative output denominator. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, Definition 2.1]
The interpolation points and evaluation point are held fixed; only the function data are perturbed. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, Section 2 opening paragraph]
The perturbation hypothesis is componentwise: |Delta f_j| <= epsilon|f_j| for every j. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, componentwise convention and Definition 2.1]
conclusions: cond(x,n,f) = (sum_{j=0}^n |ell_j(x)f_j|)/|p_n(x)|. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, Lemma 2.2 and equation (2.2)]
For every Delta f with |Delta f| <= epsilon|f|, |p_f(x)-p_{f+Delta f}(x)|/|p_f(x)| <= cond(x,n,f) epsilon. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, Lemma 2.2 second display]
The supremal numerator bound is attained by choosing Delta f_j = epsilon sign(ell_j(x))|f_j|. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, proof of Lemma 2.2]
definitions_and_conventions: p_f(x) is alternate notation for p_n(x) emphasizing dependence on the varying data vector f. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, Section 2 opening paragraph]
p_n(x) = sum_{j=0}^n f_j ell_j(x). [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, equation (2.1)]
ell_j(x) = (product over k=0:n, k != j, of (x-x_k))/(product over k=0:n, k != j, of (x_j-x_k)). [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, equation (2.1)]
Vector inequalities are interpreted componentwise. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, Section 2 opening paragraph]

cond(x,n,f) is defined by a relative output change divided by epsilon, maximized over a componentwise relative data-perturbation box and then limited as epsilon -> 0. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, Definition 2.1]
The n argument of cond represents dependence on the interpolation points x_j. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, sentence following Definition 2.1]
implicit_context: The result concerns sensitivity of the exact interpolation problem to perturbations of f, not perturbations of the nodes. [PDF p. 1, printed p. 547, Section 1 final paragraph; PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, Section 2 opening paragraph]
The dimension n+1 is inherited from the inclusive indexing j=0:n. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, Section 2 opening paragraph and equation (2.1)]
No separate restriction x != x_j is stated; x is only described as a fixed evaluation point. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, Section 2 opening paragraph]
No hypothesis requires each f_j to be nonzero; when f_j=0, the componentwise perturbation constraint forces Delta f_j=0. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, Definition 2.1]
statement.algorithm_linkage: Definition 2.1 and Lemma 2.2 define a condition number for the exact polynomial-interpolation problem and are not tied to a computed modified-Lagrange or barycentric algorithm; the introduction says Section 2 supplies the condition number before Sections 3 and 4 analyze those two formulae. [PDF p. 1, printed p. 547, Section 1 final paragraph; PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, Section 2 heading]
numerical_model: The selected result contains no floating-point operation, unit roundoff, or rounding-error hypothesis; its epsilon is a data-perturbation scale. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, Definition 2.1 and Lemma 2.2]
The standard floating-point model and unit roundoff u are introduced only in the following section. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 549, Section 3 standard floating-point model paragraph]
p_f(x) and p_{f+Delta f}(x) are exact interpolant values for the original and perturbed data in the Lagrange representation. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, equation (2.1) and Definition 2.1]
error_notions: Input error is componentwise relative data perturbation: |Delta f_j| <= epsilon|f_j|. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, componentwise convention and Definition 2.1]
Output error is the scalar relative change |p_f(x)-p_{f+Delta f}(x)|/|p_f(x)|. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, Definition 2.1 and Lemma 2.2 second display]

The condition number is local because it is defined through epsilon -> 0, while the lemma's displayed perturbation inequality is stated for any Delta f satisfying the componentwise bound. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, Definition 2.1 and Lemma 2.2]
norms: Scalar errors and terms use absolute value. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, Definition 2.1 and equation (2.2)]
The input set is described by componentwise absolute values and inequalities, not by a named vector norm. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, Section 2 componentwise convention and Definition 2.1]
The condition-number numerator is the sum of the termwise magnitudes |ell_j(x)f_j|, and the denominator is |p_n(x)|. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, equation (2.2)]
constants_and_indexing: All sums and Lagrange products use indices from 0 through n inclusive. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, equation (2.1) and equation (2.2)]
The product defining ell_j omits exactly the index k=j. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, equation (2.1)]
The lower-bound constant is exactly 1. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, equation (2.2)]
The perturbation inequality has exactly the multiplicative factor cond(x,n,f) epsilon, with no additional n-dependent constant. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, Lemma 2.2 second display]
higher_order_terms: No big-O or omitted higher-order term occurs in Definition 2.1, equation (2.2), or the perturbation bound; the condition-number identity and inequality are stated exactly. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, Definition 2.1 and Lemma 2.2]
exceptional_values: The condition number is defined only when p_n(x) != 0; the passage makes no claim for a zero interpolant value at x. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, Definition 2.1]
The nodes must be distinct, which makes the denominators in ell_j well-defined. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, Section 2 opening paragraph and equation (2.1)]
The passage does not exclude evaluating at an interpolation node x=x_i. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, Section 2 opening paragraph and equation (2.1)]
Individual zero data values are allowed by the stated hypotheses, although their admissible perturbation components must then be zero. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, Definition 2.1]

The interpolant and Lagrange basis must be related exactly by equation (2.1). [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, equation (2.1)]

The result includes the finite perturbation bound for every admissible Delta f. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, Lemma 2.2 second display]

ambiguities.issue: The selected passage does not explicitly state the scalar domain of x_j, x, and f_j. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, Section 2 and Lemma 2.2]
ambiguities.evidence: The proof uses sign(ell_j(x)), which naturally indicates real scalars, but no explicit real-domain declaration appears in the cited passage. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, proof of Lemma 2.2]
ambiguities.impact: A real formalization follows the printed attainment witness directly; a complex formalization would require a phase or conjugation-aware replacement not stated by the paper. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, proof of Lemma 2.2]

ambiguities.issue: The proof prints a sign-inconsistent linearity identity. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, proof of Lemma 2.2]
ambiguities.evidence: It writes p_f(x)-p_{f+Delta f}(x) = sum_j ell_j(x)Delta f_j, whereas equation (2.1) algebraically gives the negative of that sum. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, equation (2.1) and proof of Lemma 2.2]
ambiguities.impact: The discrepancy does not affect the absolute-value condition number, inequality, or attaining magnitude, but a literal formalization of the intermediate signed identity would be false. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, Definition 2.1, equation (2.2), and proof of Lemma 2.2]

ambiguities.issue: The direction of the limit epsilon -> 0 is not marked explicitly as one-sided. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, Definition 2.1]
ambiguities.evidence: Definition 2.1 displays epsilon -> 0 while using epsilon as the nonnegative radius in |Delta f| <= epsilon|f|. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, Definition 2.1]
ambiguities.impact: The natural reading is epsilon -> 0 through positive values, but that direction is inherited from the perturbation-radius role rather than printed as epsilon -> 0+. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, Definition 2.1]

ambiguities.issue: The paper does not define sign(0). [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, proof of Lemma 2.2]
ambiguities.evidence: The attaining perturbation is stated uniformly as Delta f_j = epsilon sign(ell_j(x))|f_j|, including possible indices with ell_j(x)=0. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, proof of Lemma 2.2]
ambiguities.impact: Any conventional choice yielding Delta f_j=0 when ell_j(x)=0 preserves attainment, but the convention itself is unstated. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, proof of Lemma 2.2]

ambiguities.issue: The passage uses degree and range notation without separately declaring the type of n. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, Section 2 opening paragraph]
ambiguities.evidence: It says degree at most n and indexes j=0:n, conventionally implying a nonnegative integer n. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, Section 2 opening paragraph]
ambiguities.impact: A formal statement must make n a natural number, although this is conventional mathematical context rather than an explicit binder in the passage. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, Section 2 opening paragraph]

contract_plain_english: Fix n+1 distinct interpolation nodes, a fixed evaluation point x, and data f defining the exact degree-at-most-n Lagrange interpolant p_n; only f is perturbed. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, Section 2 opening paragraph and equation (2.1)] When p_n(x) is nonzero, the componentwise relative condition number is the limiting worst-case relative change in p_n(x) under |Delta f| <= epsilon|f|. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, Definition 2.1] It is exactly sum_j |ell_j(x)f_j|/|p_n(x)|, is at least 1, and bounds every admissible relative output change by cond(x,n,f) epsilon. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, Lemma 2.2 and equation (2.2)] The worst-case magnitude is attained by the sign-aligned perturbation Delta f_j = epsilon sign(ell_j(x))|f_j|. [PDF p. 2, printed p. 548, proof of Lemma 2.2] This is an exact problem-sensitivity result, not a floating-point or algorithm-specific computed-error statement. [PDF p. 1, printed p. 547, Section 1 final paragraph; PDF p. 3, printed p. 549, Section 3 standard floating-point model paragraph]
